card.say: The PagingSource is on the board now, so the repository can load one page at a time. Next I'll build the Pager with it and expose the flow.
card.type: add@: private val pager = Pager( ⏎     config = PagingConfig(pageSize = 20, enablePlaceholders = false), ⏎     pagingSourceFactory = { FeedPagingSource(api) } ⏎ ) ⏎  ⏎ val feed = pager.flow.cachedIn(viewModelScope)

card.problem: Design the feed screen data loading using Paging 3 for the list
card.heard: I would rather not use Paging 3. What else could we use?
card.say: Paging 3 gives us a lot for free: it loads pages, retries errors and keeps the list state. Without it, I'd keep the same shape but write the paging myself. A simple cursor list in the ViewModel would hold the items and the next cursor. A load function would fetch one page and append it. Do you want me to switch to that?

scenarios.name: Discuss then decide: memory only? No, keep Room

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.heard: Design offline caching for the feed, use Room
card.say: Got it, Room for the local store. Before I design the tables, I want to agree on what the feed needs offline. I'd keep the last loaded pages on disk, so the user sees content right away on a cold start. Then I'd refresh from the network in the background. The main question is how we handle new items and deleted items when the user comes back online.

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.say: We could, but memory only loses everything when the app is killed. The user would open the feed offline and see nothing. Room gives us a disk copy that survives process death. I'd keep a small memory cache on top of Room for the pages on screen, so scrolling back is instant. Do you want to drop Room and go memory only, or keep Room with a memory layer?

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.say: We could, but memory only loses everything when the app is killed. The user would open the feed offline and see nothing. Room gives us a disk copy that survives process death. I'd keep a small memory cache on top of Room for the pages on screen, so scrolling back is instant. Do you want to drop Room and go memory only, or keep Room with a memory layer?

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.adopted: Keep Room, add a memory cache in front of it
card.say: Okay, Room stays. I'll put a small memory cache in front of it for the pages on screen. The feed reads from memory first, then Room, then the network. Each page we load gets saved to Room, so the next open works offline.
card.type: replace@FeedCache: class FeedCache( ⏎     private val dao: FeedDao, ⏎     private val api: FeedApi ⏎ ) { ⏎     private val memory = LinkedHashMap<Int, List<Post>>() ⏎  ⏎     suspend fun page(index: Int): List<Post> { ⏎         memory[index]?.let { return it } ⏎         dao.page(index)?.let { ⏎             memory[index] = it ⏎             return it ⏎         } ⏎         val fresh = api.page(index) ⏎         dao.save(index, fresh) ⏎         memory[index] = fresh ⏎         return fresh ⏎     } ⏎ }
card.then: Next I'd show the page as stale data first, then refresh it in the background.
